log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 26% BRING: incineroar, 20% BRING: dragapult, 16% BRING: toxapex
Pick 2: 26% BRING: gholdengo, 23% BRING: dragapult, 19% BRING: toxapex
Pick 3: 29% BRING: dragapult, 27% BRING: corviknight, 24% BRING: toxapex

Team preview: I'm bringing Incineroar (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot for support), Garchomp (Mega threat with Swords Dance), and Gholdengo (strong special attacker). Opponent has Aegislash, Gholdengo, Corviknight, Toxapex, Dragapult, and Incineroar, so expect Dragapult to outspeed and Toxapex to wall. Lead Incineroar to Fake Out or Intimidate. Save Garchomp Mega for a clean sweep setup.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 from our team against their aegislash, gholdengo, corviknight, toxapex, dragapult, incineroar lineup. Incineroar and Garchomp seem like strong picks, and I'm weighing Corviknight for its defensive utility against their Dragapult.

I'll settle on incineroar, garchomp, and gholdengo for a mix of physical pressure, intimidate, and strong special attacking power.

decisions.thought: 59% MOVE: fakeout, 12% MOVE: willowisp, 10% MOVE: crunch

Opponent team: Aegislash, Gholdengo, Corviknight, Toxapex, Dragapult, Incineroar. Their Incineroar also Intimidated us. Turn 1: Fake Out their Incineroar for free damage and a flinch. Dragapult is the main speed threat; Garchomp Mega with Swords Dance is my sweeper. Keep Incineroar for Parting Shot and Intimidate support later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Fake Out is a safe lead move here since Incineroar is full health and it's turn one, so I'll go with that for the guaranteed flinch.

decisions.thought: 27% MOVE: willowisp, 24% MOVE: crunch, 20% SWITCH: gholdengo

Opponent has Incineroar (Life Orb, Atk -1, now 90%) and has used its Fake Out. Their remaining possible threats are Aegislash, Gholdengo, Corviknight, Toxapex, and Dragapult. Dragapult is the main speed threat. Plan: Parting Shot now to bring in Garchomp, then Mega Garchomp and Swords Dance to sweep. Flare Blitz is resisted by their Fire-type Incineroar, so avoid it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 179/202 while the opponent's is at 90% with Life Orb and an Atk drop, and since it already used Fake Out this turn it can't repeat that trick unless it switches out. I'm considering bringing in Garchomp as a strong threat here.

Garchomp takes Fire moves at neutral and has Rough Skin to punish contact, so switching it in looks safe, especially since Flare Blitz would be resisted if I stayed in with Incineroar instead. Using Parting Shot is the better play though -- it drops the opponent's Incineroar further while safely bringing in Garchomp, setting up for a Mega Evolution next turn.

decisions.thought: Opp Incineroar (Life Orb, Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp, Fake Out) burned/weakened: my Incineroar Atk -1 from Intimidate-swap. Parting Shot used; switching to Garchomp now. Plan: Mega Garchomp, Swords Dance sweep. Watch Dragapult (fast, possible Ghost/Dragon), Toxapex walls physical, Aegislash, Gholdengo, Corviknight still unseen. Garchomp is burned-risk; avoid Flare Blitz.
33% SWITCH: gholdengo, 24% SWITCH: dragapult, 21% MOVE: protect

Opponent Incineroar (Life Orb, 90% HP, Atk -2, SpA -1 from my Intimidate and Parting Shot) is slower than Garchomp. Earthquake is super effective and should KO it without Mega. I'm saving Mega Garchomp for a later threat, since Dragapult, Corviknight, Toxapex, Aegislash and Gholdengo remain. Their Incineroar may have Fake Out and Will-O-Wisp, so burn risk applies to Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Incineroar is weakened at 90% with stat drops from Parting Shot and intimidate, and since Garchomp outspeeds it, Earthquake should land as a super-effective hit that likely finishes it off.

decisions.thought: 25% MOVE: recover, 18% SWITCH: dragapult, 16% MOVE: shadowball

Garchomp (faster than every opposing Pokémon except possibly Dragapult) is about to KO the 12% Gholdengo with a non-Mega Earthquake. I'm holding Mega Garchomp for a later threat such as Dragapult or Corviknight. Opponent known so far: Incineroar (Life Orb, Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp, Fake Out, now at 90%, Atk -2, SpA -1). Gholdengo has Good as Gold, so status moves like Will-O-Wisp can't hit it. Remaining unseen: Aegislash, Corviknight, Toxapex, Dragapult (one of them comes in). Watch Garchomp's burn risk from Incineroar.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Gholdengo is at 12% and Garchomp outspeeds it, so earthquake should finish it off since steel types are weak to ground. Garchomp has plenty of HP and isn't affected by Gholdengo's status immunity here since earthquake is physical — I'll just go with earthquake.

decisions.thought: 30% MOVE: shadowball, 26% MOVE: dragonclaw, 19% MOVE: uturn

Opponent's Gholdengo is down. Their remaining known threats are Dragapult (fast, Dragon/Ghost, unknown item) and Incineroar (Life Orb, Will-O-Wisp, Fake Out, Intimidate, about 90% HP). Dragapult is faster than or close to my Garchomp, so I'm attacking now with Mega Garchomp's super-effective Dragon Claw. Mega Garchomp may also set sand via Sand Force. Earthquake is neutral against Dragapult, so Dragon Claw is the better hit. Keep Incineroar in reserve; avoid Flare Blitz burn risk.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragapult is Dragon/Ghost, so Earthquake hits neutrally, while Dragon Claw gets a same-type boost against its Dragon typing but is only neutral against the Ghost part.

Dragapult is quite fast and could outspeed Garchomp, threatening heavy damage with its own Dragon moves, though Garchomp's bulk gives it some room. Mega Garchomp's Sand Force ability would boost both Earthquake and a potential Dragon Claw under self-made sand, and the super-effective Dragon Claw likely deals solid damage, maybe 60-70%, making it a strong attacking option here.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: 32% MOVE: crunch, 25% MOVE: protect, 23% MOVE: willowisp

Opponent Incineroar (Life Orb, 90% HP, Fake Out, Will-O-Wisp, Intimidate) is slower than my Mega Garchomp (158 Speed). Earthquake is super effective and should KO it before it acts. After that, the opponent's remaining known threat is Aegislash, Corviknight, or Toxapex, which I haven't seen yet. Gholdengo (Life Orb, Nasty Plot, Make It Rain) is my backup. Watch for Corviknight and Toxapex: Dragon Claw or Stone Edge may be needed for those.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at 90% HP, roughly 182 max HP, facing Garchomp Mega with its Attack dropped by one stage. Earthquake is doubly effective against the Fire/Dark typing since Ground hits Fire hard, and with STAB plus that 2x effectiveness against a lowered Attack stat of about 148, I'm checking if the 100 base power hit is enough to take it down.

Garchomp outspeeds, so going in with Earthquake should either secure the KO or leave it very low, and the Life Orb recoil doesn't matter here since it's a clearly winning move.
